articleTitle: Sliding mode controller for the boost inverter
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: The sliding mode control theory is applied to a sinusoidal output voltage boost inverter with linear load. The boost inverter is intended to be used in UPS design, whenever an AC voltage larger than the DC link voltage is needed, with no need of a second power conversion stage. Operation, control strategy, simulation and experimental results are included in this paper.

articleTitle: Steady-state frequency analysis of the "LLC" resonant inverter for induction heating
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: In this paper, the main steady-state frequency properties of the LLC circuit are described. The advantage of its use on induction heating applications is proved, in contrast with the SRI (series resonant inverter). This analysis will allow the future design of a frequency control strategy for the inverter. Finally, a simple design algorithm is proposed, which satisfies the power specifications and limits the stress current in the switches.

articleTitle: Optimizing core and winding design in high frequency transformers
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: A design methodology is presented which is based on a restatement of the traditional transformer equations to include nonsinusoidal switching waveforms and high frequency skin and proximity effects. Core selection is determined by the optimum throughput of energy with minimum losses. Winding layout is optimised to minimise skin and proximity effects. Suitable approximations are presented to simplify calculations. A detailed design or a push-pull converter is presented to illustrate the methodology.

articleTitle: Microcontroller-based switch for three-phase transformer inrush current minimization
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for the minimization of three-phase transformer inrush current in the case of sustained switching-on operations. First, a simple mathematical model of the three-phase transformer was derived taking the residual flux and the switching-on instant into consideration. A table of optimum switching-on instants corresponding to different residual fluxes was constructed for a specified three-phase transformer. Based on an 8031 microcontroller a controlled-switch was built using the mentioned table. Experimental results using the controlled-switch were obtained and compared with others found by direct switching-on which gave good results.

articleTitle: Elimination of dead time effects in three phase inverters
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: In the design of inverters it is necessary to include a "dead time" in switching signals in order to avoid the simultaneous conduction of the devices on the same electrical trajectory or leg. Incorporation of this dead time produces a modification on commutation real angles with respect to the theoreticals. In this paper, an analysis and compensation of the dead time effects in three phase inverters is presented. It is shown that the dead time generates a decrease in the magnitude voltage of the harmonic fundamental and an increase in the low order harmonics. The paper also includes the implementation of a technique to compensate the dead time effect through the sensing current; this technique is applicable to sinusoidal and programmed PWM techniques. The analysis and compensation of the dead time are validated by means of experimental results in a three phase inverter for an induction motor drive, and a three phase inverter for UPS.

articleTitle: Simplifying the design of a DCM boost PFP
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper presents a simplified approach to the design of a PWM-DCM boost power factor preregulator. Using a simplified equation which represents a good approximation of the original equation makes it simpler to determine the inductance value as well as to obtain a representative small-signal model for the converter. The approach is validated by simulation and experimentation.

articleTitle: Modeling of magnetic components based on finite element techniques
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper describes a full procedure to model magnetic components based on finite element analysis (FEA) techniques and practical aspects of the FEA tool are also considered. The model used is frequency dependent and of distributed effects. This model is particularly useful for magnetic components working with nonsinusoidal wave-forms (it can adequately take into account the harmonics) and when the currents do not flow at the same time in the windings (it can take into account separately the winding impedances). This paper is an overview of a set of papers previously published.

articleTitle: Speed control of ultrasonic motors using fuzzy neural network
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper presents a speed control system for ultrasonic motors by PI (proportional and integral) control which has auto-tuning structure based reasoning realized by a neural network. The speed characteristics of the ultrasonic motor vary with temperature and applied load torque, therefore, adjusting the control gains of the PI controller is necessary in order to obtain fine speed control performance. The proposed control scheme can incorporate the operators's knowledge in a speed controller using fuzzy reasoning, furthermore, it can compensate the speed characteristic variations of the motor by online learning. The usefulness and validity of the proposed control scheme is examined by experiments.

articleTitle: Power factor preregulators employing the flyback and zeta converters in FM mode
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: The flyback and zeta converters can work as power factor preregulators (PFP). These converters can be designed to obtain unitary power factor, that is, they are resistance emulators. In this paper, a method for high frequency electromagnetic interference reduction using the frequency modulation (FM) approach is described for these converters. Results show that a reduction of conducted electromagnetic interferences (EMI) generated by these converters is possible using the FM technique. The price for this EMI reduction is a small reduction in the power factor (PF).

articleTitle: A family of soft-switching DC-DC power converters to high power applications
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper presents a family of soft-switching DC-DC power converters, which is suitable for high power applications using IGBTs. These converters present the following characteristics: commutation at zero-current (turn-on and turn-off) for all active switches without overvoltage and overcurrent, commutation at zero-voltage for the free-wheeling diode, and PWM operating at constant frequency. Small power rated auxiliary components can be used. To verify the feasibility of the proposed family of soft-switching DC-DC power converters, the ZCS-PWM boost converter is analyzed. Operating principle, commutation analysis and features are described and verified by experimental results obtained from a prototype operating at 40 kHz, rated at 155 V input voltage and 1.1 kW output power. The measured efficiency to full load was about 98%.

articleTitle: Electronic regulation by the load of the electrical variables and speed of asynchronous micro turbogenerators
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: The paper shows how a single DC-DC converter can advantageously replace the conventional mechanical controllers to regulate, at the same time, speed and the electrical variables (either voltage, current or power). The rotation of the turbogenerator is kept within certain limits through modulation of the active power and using the inherent voltage characteristics of the asynchronous generators. The control is based on a current diversion from the main load to a secondary load using a very conventional DC-DC converter connected in parallel to the main load. Everything happens in such a way that the main load current becomes approximately independent of the generator current changes and vice-versa. The excess of current may be recovered in a secondary plant with large time constant such as heating, cooling, water irrigation, backpumping scheme or battery charging.

articleTitle: A new experimental method to desegregate the harmonic power produced by thyristor AC/DC three phase converters
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper introduces a new experimental method that desegregates the harmonic power in the AC coupling point of thyristor pulse controlled AC/DC three phase power converters, during the occurrence of voltage unbalances in the AC source that feeds the converter. This method of measurement resolves the total harmonic power into two orthogonal harmonic components, whose existence is theoretically demonstrated for sinusoidal voltage and nonsinusoidal current conditions. A scaled down AC/DC/AC transmission link physical model that includes characteristic harmonics passive filtering, and AC primary side weakening facilities is used for measurement purposes. Balanced and unbalanced voltage conditions are also readily simulated in this physical model. The two 3-phase converters linked by a lumped parameters transmission line that constitute the AC/DC/AC system can act either as rectifier or inverter, depending upon the firing angle control imposed on the converter's valves. The two orthogonal harmonic components, that were given by the authors the names of characteristic harmonic power and noncharacteristic harmonic power, have not been previously desegregated neither theoretically nor experimentally. The relevance of this paper may be better judged in the framework of research efforts that have been undertaken to overcome the harmonic content of a noncharacteristic nature. These kind of harmonic effects are present during the steady state that follows an asymmetrical AC disturbance in the coupling point of AC/DC three phase power converters. The paper includes extensive results on such phenomena.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis between two proposed uses of the line inter-phase transformer in 12 pulse three phase rectifiers
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: In this paper a comparative study between two proposed uses of the line inter-phase transformer (LIT), as a passive solution to improve the input current shape in very high power three phase systems, is presented . By using the LIT, in 12 pulse operations, an input current shaping without the 5th and 7th harmonics is obtained. Experimental results, theoretical analysis and numerical simulation are presented to accomplish the comparison.

articleTitle: Harmonic distortion caused by suburban and underground rolling stock with DC motors
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: The paper presents the problem of disturbances caused by the converters of electric traction vehicles with DC motors. Although these type of rolling stock have been used since the 1970s, the problem is still vital, especially in countries without experience with modern electric traction. When a project to introduce new types of rolling stock in a suburban railway or underground line is carried out, analyses have to be done in order to estimate the electromagnetic disturbances which could be caused by the vehicles' converters, especially when the existing signalling and control system is of an old type. The authors discuss the problems of harmonic disturbance and then discuss the PC-NAP simulation tool used for simulating the harmonic disturbances in the whole traction system.

articleTitle: Parameters variation influence in class E amplifiers used as ballast for fluorescent lamps
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: The class E amplifier presents advantages such as: low weight, size and components number, simple structure, high efficiency, etc. which make very interesting its application in ballasts for fluorescent lamps. However, the principal disadvantage that this topology presents is the complexity of its design, since in the class E amplifier all the elements are interrelated. In this paper an analysis of the parameters variation influence in the design and operation of the class E amplifier used as ballast for fluorescent lamps is presented. Furthermore, experimental results of a prototype of 12 V for 21 W lamps are also included.

articleTitle: A novel PWM inverter control circuitry for induction heating
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: In induction heating applications, the heating coils may have different types for different loads. A suitable control method is often needed to let the power electronic circuit working in most fittable condition to supply power to the load. In this paper, a simple novel control strategy for induction heating is described. The most outstanding advantage of this method is a design of a simple PWM (pulse-width-modulation) gate signal driving circuitry for easily dead time setting, ZVS (zero voltage switching) operation, and less components architecture. Another advantage of this technique is using a very simple method to alternate the two complementary PWM output signals into different switching devices in heating period for balancing the operation duty cycles.

articleTitle: Calculated performance of AC motors in a single-phase to three-phase converter application
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: In this paper the performance of induction motors operating with a single-phase to three-phase converter is analyzed. Usually, the motor is connected in open-delta, one side is fed by the AC supply, and the other side by a PWM waveform; as a result, the motor operates under unbalanced conditions. The effect of this unbalance is evaluated taking into account the percent of voltage unbalance, as defined by NEMA standards; the reduction of the torque; the additional rotor losses, and the overheating of the motor. For evaluation purposes, a programmed PWM technique and a class B, 3/4 HP induction motor are used.

articleTitle: Harmonic reduction in low-cost power supplies
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: Power electronic loads inject harmonic currents into the utility system. The large increase of power consumption will inevitably lead to deteriorating power quality due to the popularity of switch-mode power electronic equipment. Designers must satisfy two requirements. First obtain nearly sinusoidal line currents to comply with the international standard IEC 1000-3-2, and second achieve low cost, high operating efficiency and reliability to be competitive in the marketplace. In this paper we analyze the way to reduce the size and cost of the passive filters and still provide compliance with the international harmonic reduction regulations for low-power and low-cost applications.

articleTitle: Spectral analysis of switching converters using a generalized transfer function
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: In this paper a sampled-data method for the spectral analysis of DC-DC and DC-AC switching converters (SCs) is presented. It is specifically oriented to the detection of the incoming switching and modulation harmonics connected to the different types of operation of DC-DC and DC-AC SCs. The method is not based on the small-signal assumption and the computation of the spectral components of any waveform with arbitrary accuracy is carried out using a generalized transfer function, describing the spectral properties of the converters modelled as time-varying discrete-time systems. Some examples of application are presented concerning DC-DC and DC-AC converters.

articleTitle: Modeling and control of a three-phase high power factor PWM-ZVS power supply with a single power stage
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper presents the modeling and control of the three-phase high power factor PWM-ZVS power supply with a single power stage presented previously by te authors (see Proc. PESC, Taipei, Taiwan, IEEE, p.356-62, 1994). A small signals model of the converter is developed by using the PWM switch equivalent circuit technique. The transfer function which describes the dynamic behavior of the converter is obtained from the model. A complete method to calculate the parameters and coefficients of the developed model, as well as the control systems are presented. Simulations confirm the theoretical results.

articleTitle: A novel technique for variable-capacitor filter. I. AC current harmonic control
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper introduces a novel technique for controlling current harmonics in power supply converter systems. A variable characteristics capacitive active filter is proposed and is used to control the AC current harmonics generated by a standard AC/DC converter with resistive load and a smoothing capacitor. The idea of the proposed filter is to use a combination of capacitors and switches to form a circuit which varies its capacitance with time. The filter will then generate harmonics in antiphase with the harmonics generated by the nonlinear load. Simulation and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Influence of the firing angle control in the harmonic generation of thyristor pulse controlled AC/DC/AC systems
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper presents some selected results of experimentally based research to observe the firing angle control influence on the harmonic level generated by two 6-pulse-controlled three phase converters, connected in an AC/DC/AC configuration. The sending-end of this scheme is constituted by a rectifier, while the reception-end is made up by a three phase converter acting in its inverter mode of operation. Thus, such harmonic phenomena as the one presented in a weak AC line feeding electrochemical and electrometallurgical industries is readily simulated. Also the harmonic effects of network asymmetries in the reception-end of HVDC transmission links, can be easily implemented in this physical model. The paper includes selected graphs showing the dependence of both individual harmonic voltages and currents on the firing angles of rectifier and inverter operations. The firing angle control impact is observed for both filtered and nonfiltered harmonic phenomena.

articleTitle: LTR observers for induction motor drives
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: A new electromagnetic state observer, based on the concept of loop transfer recovery (LTR), is presented. The simplicity of induction motor electromagnetic dynamics in a complex variable has made it possible to deduce an observer which presents an optimal response to perturbations located at the input of the plant and almost insensitive to stator resistance and inductance variations.

articleTitle: Search for optimum number of turns of switched reluctance motor
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper presents a method for selecting the optimum number of turns per phase winding of the SR motor with a given magnetic configuration and specified (required) operating conditions in terms of the output power and speed. The method is based on comparing performances predicted iteratively for hypothetical motors with different number of turns. Each iteration includes: (i) transforming the initial input data (magnetisation characteristics and phase winding resistance) for the mathematical model of the SR motor, to take into account the change of number of turns; and (ii) search for the optimum values of control variables which give maximum efficiency at the required output power and speed.

articleTitle: Generalized approach to robust feedforward control and its application to servo control
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: In this paper, we propose a robust feedforward control scheme for a SISO system. Our control scheme consists of a model-based feedforward controller and stabilizing feedback controller. The feedforward controller is designed such that the output of the nominal plant tracks perfectly the reference input with the desired dynamic characteristics. We then design a feedback controller so as to achieve the suppression of all the disturbances including internal disturbances due to system uncertainties as well as external disturbances. Finally, by applying our controller to a servo control system, we demonstrate some advantages of our control scheme over the conventional ones through computer simulations and experimental results.

articleTitle: Frequency domain analysis of DC-DC converters with internally controlled switching instants
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: A sampled-data method for determining the frequency responses of DC-DC switching converters (SCs) within the f/sub s//2 limit is proposed in this paper. The method is conceived to treat DC-DC SCs operating in any mode which involves internally controlled switching instants (ICSI), regardless of their number and location. The formulation of the method is based on the recursive use of the relation between the state at neighbouring switching instants within the switching period. Some examples of applications to DC-DC SCs are proposed, including the comparisons between the forecastings of the method, the experimental measurements and the results obtained by means of other techniques of analysis.

articleTitle: Induction motor drive parameters identification
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: The paper deals with real-time identification of the rotor parameters of the induction motor drive. The model reference adaptative control technique has been used for synthesising two identifiers. An appropriate choice of the reference model allows a Lyapunov function to be built by means of which the updating law of the rotor time constant can be found. A higher order identifier is also synthesised using the hyperstability approach which allows real-time updating of two rotor parameters. The persistent exciting property of the input vector assures the parameters convergence. Using a DSP-based system (TMS320C30), having 30 MHz clock frequency, a few experiments are conducted for testing the proposed identifiers performance in the case of a CRPWM inverter supplied drive.

articleTitle: IGBT modelling using HSPICE
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper discusses a simple method for IGBT modelling, which requires only circuit element parameters and does not involve the user in implementing mathematical equations. The structure of the model is comprised of a bipolar junction transistor (BJT) combined with a metal oxide field effect/transistor (MOSFET). The parameters are estimated using an optimization algorithm in HSPICE and the device test data. Results showing a close fit of model output to the experimental data are presented.

articleTitle: A robust load current compensation method for PWM power converter
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new nonlinear DC link voltage control scheme, which is based on a nonlinear load current observer, for voltage type PWM power converter. The load current observer is designed by using the full nonlinear converter model and our converter control scheme does not require any additional sensing device. Therefore, the converter adopting our new controller can provide fast and precise voltage regulation and can be made cheap and small. To demonstrate the practical use of our control method, we present various experimental results as well as mathematical performance analysis.

articleTitle: Study on the parameter identification for induction motors
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: In this paper, the induction motor control system with high dynamic performance by means of decoupling control and motor parameter adaptation is presented. For power efficiency control or field weakening, the rotor flux may be reduced at light loads. Motor inductances depend on rotor flux but not on machine temperature. So, if the rotor flux is changed, the motor inductances should also be changed according to the rotor flux commands. On the other hand, the rotor resistance varies greatly with the machine temperature. The value of rotor resistance must be estimated instantly during the operation. We present novel identification algorithms for motor inductances and rotor resistance. Our identification algorithms are computationally simple and have very small identification errors.

articleTitle: Sensorless vector control of brushless DC motors based on instantaneous power
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper presents a new control strategy for a brushless DC motor drive without position and speed sensors. The rotor position is calculated from the model position and the position error between rotor and model position. The position error cannot be detected directly, however, it can be estimated by the information of the instantaneous power which is calculated by the terminal voltages and currents transformed to the motor axis. The rotor speed can also be calculated in a similar way. The useful features and validity of this proposed sensorless control scheme is confirmed by computer simulations.

articleTitle: Simple robust speed control scheme for DC servomotors using fuzzy reasoning
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: The speed control methods using disturbance torque observer have been investigated by many researchers. However, it is difficult to use an observer in a real machine, because the observer has several disadvantages: the selection of the observer's poles, the complexity of the calculation, and so on. We use a simple estimation mechanism instead of the observer to estimate the disturbance torque. However, this simple mechanism has estimation error for disturbance torque, and the error detracts from the control performance. Thus, we proposed the robust speed control method for DC servomotors considering the estimation error. In order to compensate the estimation error, we combine the equivalent disturbance torque estimator and a feedback controller. The influence of the estimation error is restrained by the feedback controller introducing fuzzy reasoning. The simulation and experimental results confirm the validity of the proposed control technique.

articleTitle: Economical circuit of a three-phase PWM AC power controller with a new control algorithm without "dead time"
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: In this paper a new economical control algorithm of a three-phase PWM AC power controller with (2+2) transistorized switches has been discussed. The switching frequency of the described PWM AC power controller is f/sub s//spl Gt/f, where: f=frequency of the supply voltage. Test results of this power controller using a traditional and a new control algorithm has been described. The new algorithm has been realized in two ways. In the first variant, instantaneous values of the load current in two phases are exclusively measured. In the second variant, two line-to-line output voltages are additionally measured.

articleTitle: Parallel power regulation techniques for resonant converters
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: Parallel power regulation techniques increase the efficiency of power converters, achieving regulation by handling only a percentage of the power transmitted from the input to the output, in contrast to classical regulation schemes where all the power flow is controlled in order to regulate the output. Our work describes a procedure to parallel regulate high efficiency resonant converters that operate at constant frequency and constant duty cycle and that otherwise should be regulated using pre-regulation or post-regulation principles. As a result, efficiency increments of up to 6% are obtained when providing output regulation against 20% input variation.

articleTitle: A control system for high speed operation of the permanent magnet synchronous motor
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: A complete digital control system to improve the high speed operation of the interior type permanent magnet synchronous motor is presented, This control scheme allows for a smooth transition of the motor into and out of the flux weakening mode, very fast response and adjustment to the current and voltage saturation limits of the motor and inverter. The core of the control system consists of three PI regulators plus three look-up tables, thus enabling the microprocessor implementation with low sampling times. The whole drive system including a space vector modulator is simulated, thus proving the feasibility of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Alternatives for increasing the output power in an integrated battery charger/discharger topology
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: Distributed power supply systems (DPS) are an attractive solution to meet the requirements demanded from a power supply. However, it has some drawbacks which must be overcome. An integrated battery charger/discharger topology is a good solution in order to improve the structures already existent. The goal is increase the maximum output power of an integrated battery charger/discharger because the output power capability is limited in this topology by the switch current stress. This paper address these topics in order to overcome the limitation mentioned above. In this paper new alternatives are evaluated, which maintain the characteristics of power factor correction and battery galvanic isolation in a simple structure. It has a higher efficiency than solutions previously developed.

articleTitle: Steady state analysis of a high power factor ballast for fluorescent lamps
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: The steady state operation modes and the commutation zones of a single stage, high power factor ballast are studied. A design criteria to implement the ballast is given. Experimental results verify the theoretical study.

articleTitle: Conception, design and experimental results of a bipolar power supply for trimming magnets
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: An alternative approach to the design of a high-efficiency bipolar power supply is to combine the features of a switching regulator with those of a linear regulator. In this paper, we use as linear regulator, a class-AB linear amplifier that works like a linear post-regulator in the linear region. This new topology is suitable for low power levels and has the advantages of a high efficiency, good audiosusceptibility and frequency response.

articleTitle: Field angle adaptation [induction motors]
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: In systems without converters for measuring the stator voltages, only reduced order observers based on the current equation are seen. Full order rotor flux observers are not applicable because stator voltage measurements are used. This problem is managed in this paper by an adaptive approach leading to a completely new method called field angle adaptation (FAA). The new contribution to the conventional current control system in rotor field oriented dq-coordinates is a signal added to the field angle in the transformation from rotor field coordinates to stator fixed coordinates. This signal adapts the field angle estimate to the correct rotor field angle in an induction motor.

articleTitle: Experimental results of speed control in electrical machines using fuzzy logic controllers
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper deals with some results obtained from fuzzy logic controllers (FLC) applied to a DC motor and an AC three-phase motor. Dynamic parameters such as speed, accuracy and stability are evaluated, and results of terminal characteristics are also presented.

articleTitle: HPF electronic ballast for a 110 W fluorescent lamp
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: This paper presents a high power factor electronic ballast to drive a 110 W fluorescent lamp. The proposed ballast is based on a single power processing stage formed by a half bridge converter. High power factor is obtained by a nonconventional boost converter operating at critical conduction mode. The fluorescent lamp is driven by a self-oscillation series-parallel resonant converter operating above the resonant frequency to provide zero voltage switching. Experimental results have been obtained for a 110 W fluorescent lamp operating at 50 kHz switching frequency and 220 V line voltage.

articleTitle: Analysis and design considerations of a novel integrated SMPS with battery backup and power factor correction
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: Uninterruptible energy is highly appreciated in applications such as personal computers, medical equipment, workstations, portable measurement equipment, and others. Besides, the appearance of standards about the quality of demanded line current for this equipment has been the cause of development of new power supply schemes capable of integrating battery backup and power factor correction in simple structures which offer both, low cost and size alternatives. This paper describes a novel and simple structure which offers power factor correction and battery backup capability. The proposed structure has excellent characteristics in terms of cost, size and efficiency, taking into account the reduced number of components. Experimental results of an experimental prototype of the proposed converter are included too.

articleTitle: New generator static exciter with boost function
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: A new generator static exciter with boost function (boost-buck chopper exciter) is proposed to overcome the lack of field forcing capability of the conventional bus fed exciter which can not maintain the generator terminal voltage under a fault condition. The validity of the proposed exciter is verified using computer simulation. The proposed exciter has the capability to supply the ceiling current even if the exciter input voltage decreases to 55% of the rated voltage compared with that of conventional bus fed exciter at normal condition. The function of the proposed exciter is tested and verified using voltage and load step function tests on the 25 kVA synchronous generator driven by a DC motor.

articleTitle: Design criteria for zero-current-switched quasi-resonant SEPIC used as power factor pre-regulator with voltage follower control
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: Nowadays it is needed to count with small size and high efficiency power factor pre-regulator (PFP). According to the experimental results, the zero-current-switched quasi-resonant SEPIC (ZCS-QR SEPIC) used as PFP with voltage follower control seems to be a good choice to solve the problem mentioned above. This study gives the qualitative and quantitative criteria for the most favourable design of this type of PFP.

articleTitle: A study of the two-input DC-to-DC switching post-regulators
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: A study of the two-input post-regulators is carried out in this paper. In these post-regulators, only a part of the total power undergoes a switching conversion process, whereas the remainder of the power comes up to the load directly, with no power conversion process. Due to this fact, very high efficiency is achieved. Moreover, the stress in the semiconductors and the filter size are both much lower than in standard post-regulators. Two-input post-regulators require two-output main converters. However, many converter topologies can be easily adapted to supply two output voltages with no efficiency penalty. Two-input post-regulators can be used in many power converters. Multiple-output DC-to-DC converters and AC-to-DC power factor correctors are two good examples.

articleTitle: Index of authors
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
abstract: Presents an index of the authors whose papers are published in the conference.

articleTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
publicationTitle: V IEEE International Power Electronics Congress Technical Proceedings, CIEP 96
